findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: findCompanies, getPosition, getComputeWeek, getComputeCount, getComputeCampuses, getWeeklyIssue, getConsultingOffer · Private data: checkClaim, findCompanies, getRecentMarketCalls, getTokenPrices, getPriceSpreads, getPosition, getPrintBaseRate, getSeries, getComputeQuestions, submitConsultingInquiry · Public sink: findArticles, submitConsultingInquiry · Destructive: getComputeWeek.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: findCompanies, getPosition, getComputeWeek, getComputeCount, getComputeCampuses, getWeeklyIssue, getConsultingOffer · Private data: checkClaim, findCompanies, getRecentMarketCalls, getTokenPrices, getPriceSpreads, getPosition, getPrintBaseRate, getSeries, getComputeQuestions, submitConsultingInquiry · Public sink: findArticles, submitConsultingInquiry · Destructive: getComputeWeek

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
